Net force and acceleration: Newton's
second law
A force changes an object's motion only when the forces do not balance. This page defines the
relationship between net force, mass and acceleration.
The central idea
Newton's second law states that an object's acceleration is determined by the net external force acting
on it and by its mass. For a fixed mass, a larger net force produces a larger acceleration. For a fixed net

ΣF or F_net is the vector sum of all external forces, measured in newtons (N). m is mass in kilograms
(kg). a is acceleration in metres per second squared (m/s²). The acceleration points in the same
direction as the net force.
Worked example
A trolley has a 10 N force acting east and a 4 N force acting west.
